_about: SERIES SHELF: the American-Scandinavian Foundation's Scandinavian Classics (New York, 1914 onward), translations of Old Norse, Danish, Norwegian and Swedish books, for the volumes no other shelf holds: Brodeur's Prose Edda (1916), two Bjørnson volumes, Almqvist's Sara Videbeck and Hallström's stories; added in round 91, Tegnér's Poems (1914), A Book of Danish Verse (1922) and Munch's Norse Mythology (1926). Bellows's Poetic Edda, Holberg, Strindberg's Master Olof, Jacobsen, Lie, Sigurjónsson and the translators with their own shelves (Stork, Hollander, Björkman, Hanna Larsen) are shelved elsewhere. Each title gates on its own translator. Printings before 1931 only. US public domain. Added 2026-10-17 by lane C (round 89); Adam may veto. No uids minted.
_name_words_note: Translator names only: fetch_shelf.py treats them as the identity check. Bare 'payne' and 'palmer' are left out: other shelves (John Payne's among them) claim them.
_surname_note: Per title: the translator's name forms.

_pending.schlauch-saga-of-the-volsungs: Margaret Schlauch's The Saga of the Volsungs (American-Scandinavian Foundation, 'Copyright, 1930'; archive.org sagaofvolsungs0000marg). Waits on the 1930 ruling: the gate still treats 1930 as in copyright.

_excluded.america-of-the-fifties: America of the Fifties: Letters of Fredrika Bremer (1924) is 'selected and edited' by Adolph B. Benson, not a new translation; Mary Howitt's translations of Bremer are on mary-howitt.
_excluded.gosta-berlings-saga: Gösta Berling's Saga in the American-Scandinavian Foundation's translation (1918; the catalogue names Tudeer as translator) is left to the lagerlof shelf, whose owner lists her novels as candidates for a later batch.
